paraphrase: Chapter 16 (Kṛṣṇa to Arjuna) sets out the two endowments (sampad) with which beings are born. 16.1-3: the twenty-six marks of the divine endowment (fearlessness, purity of being, steadfastness in jñānayoga, giving, self-restraint, sacrifice, recitation, austerity, straightforwardness, non-harming, truth … absence of excessive pride). 16.4: the marks of the demonic endowment (hypocrisy, arrogance, conceit, anger, harshness, ignorance). 16.5: the divine leads to release, the demonic to bondage; Arjuna is told not to grieve, being born to the divine. 16.6: there are two creations of beings, divine and demonic; the demonic is now described at length. 16.7-18: the demonic know neither engagement nor withdrawal and have no purity, conduct or truth; they hold the world to be without truth, foundation or Lord and caused by desire (16.8); they come forth for the world's destruction, driven by insatiable desire, endless cares and unjust gain (16.9-12); their self-conceit is voiced in their own words (16.13-15) and they fall into hell (16.16); they sacrifice in name only and hate the Lord in their own and others' bodies (16.17-18). 16.19-20: the Lord casts them into demonic wombs, and they sink lower birth after birth without reaching him. 16.21-22: desire, anger and greed are the threefold gate of hell, to be abandoned; the one freed from them does what is good for the self and reaches the highest course. 16.23-24: whoever abandons the injunction of scripture for desire gains neither perfection, happiness nor the highest course; scripture is therefore Arjuna's authority on what is to be done and not done, and he should act knowing it.
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
notes: The chapter's stated purpose, read from its own close (16.21-24): the hearer, told he has the divine endowment (16.5), is to abandon the three gates and act by scripture. The chapter colophon title (not part of this edition's segments) is traditionally 'Daivāsura-sampad-vibhāga-yoga'.

original.text: asatyamapratiṣṭhaṃ te jagadāhuranīśvaram|aparasparasambhūtaṃ kimanyatkāmahaitukam

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa: They say the world is without truth (asatya), without foundation (apratiṣṭha), without a Lord (anīśvara), arisen from mutual union (aparaspara-sambhūta) — 'what else? It is caused by desire (kāma).'

paraphrase: Chapter 17 answers Arjuna's question (17.1) about the standing of those who set aside scriptural injunction yet sacrifice with faith. 17.2-4: faith is threefold, born of nature; a person is made of faith, and is what his faith is; the sāttvic worship gods, the rājasic yakṣas and rākṣasas, the tāmasic the departed and spirits. 17.5-6: those who practise terrible austerities not enjoined by scripture, tormenting the body's elements and the Lord within, are of demonic resolve. 17.7-22: food (17.8-10), sacrifice (17.11-13), austerity — of body, speech and mind (17.14-16) and by the guṇas (17.17-19) — and giving (17.20-22), each sāttvic, rājasic or tāmasic. 17.23-27: '[oṃ] tat sat', the threefold designation of Brahman by which brāhmaṇas, Vedas and sacrifices were ordained: the rites of the expounders of Brahman begin with oṃ; those seeking release act with 'tat' without aiming at fruit; 'sat' denotes reality, goodness, a praiseworthy act, steadfastness in sacrifice, austerity and giving, and action for that purpose. 17.28: what is offered, given, practised or done without faith is 'asat', of no account here or hereafter.
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Speakers: Arjuna (17.1), Kṛṣṇa (17.2-28). The chapter answers the question of 17.1 by the guṇas of faith rather than by a single verdict; its close (17.28) makes faith the condition of any act counting as 'sat'. Traditional colophon title (not in the segments): 'Śraddhātraya-vibhāga-yoga'.

paraphrase: Chapter 18 opens with Arjuna's request to know the truth of renunciation (saṃnyāsa) and relinquishment (tyāga) (18.1). 18.2-12: the two defined (laying aside desire-prompted acts; giving up the fruit of all acts), two reported views on abandoning action (18.3), Kṛṣṇa's conclusion that sacrifice, giving and austerity are to be done without attachment or fruit (18.4-6), relinquishment by the guṇas (18.7-9), the relinquisher (18.10-11), and the fruit of action after death (18.12). 18.13-18: the five factors of every act (seat, agent, instruments, activities, the divine), so that one who sees the self alone as agent does not see, while one without the sense of doership, though he slays, neither slays nor is bound (18.16-17); the impulses and constituents of action (18.18). 18.19-40: knowledge, action, agent, understanding, steadiness and happiness, each threefold by the guṇas; no being is free of the guṇas (18.40). 18.41-48: the works of the four varṇas born of their nature; perfection through one's own work offered as worship to him who pervades all; one's own dharma is better than another's. 18.49-56: through unattached understanding and renunciation to the perfection of actionlessness; the discipline (18.51-53) by which one becomes Brahman, attains supreme devotion, knows the Lord in truth and enters him; by grace the one who takes refuge attains the eternal state even while acting. 18.57-62: renounce all acts in the Lord in thought and keep thought on him; if from the sense of 'I' Arjuna refuses to fight, his nature will compel him; the Lord in the heart moves all beings; take refuge in him. 18.63-66: the secret knowledge has been told, to be reflected on before acting; then the most secret word: be devoted to me; abandoning all dharmas, take refuge in me alone; I will release you from all sins; do not grieve. 18.67-71: to whom the teaching must not be told, and the reward of teaching, studying and hearing it. 18.72-73: asked whether his delusion is gone, Arjuna answers that delusion is destroyed, memory regained by grace, doubt gone, and he will do Kṛṣṇa's word. 18.74-78: Sañjaya closes the dialogue: he heard it through Vyāsa's grace, rejoices in recalling it and Hari's form, and holds that where Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna are there are fortune, victory, prosperity and firm right conduct.
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Speakers: Arjuna (18.1, 18.73), Kṛṣṇa (18.2-72), Sañjaya to Dhṛtarāṣṭra (18.74-78). The chapter closes the whole dialogue: Arjuna's 'I will do your word' (18.73) answers his refusal 'I will not fight' (2.9), and Sañjaya's close (18.74-78) answers Dhṛtarāṣṭra's question of 1.1. Traditional colophon title (not in the segments): 'Mokṣa-saṃnyāsa-yoga'.

notes: The verse does not say which dharmas are to be abandoned or in what sense.
